text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chinese engineers expected this week in Nigeria to overhaul ailing northern Afam Thermal station and train locals on power generation and distribution.

- Shareholders of Nigeria's liquefied natural gas (LNG) project have jointly paid 3.2 billion naira out of the 6.1 billion naira required for its execution, project's chief executive officer Theo Oerlemans says.

- Slain author and rights activist Ken Saro-Wiwa's Movement for the Survival of Ogoni Peoples (MOSOP) should opt for dialogue to end crisis in volatile Ogoniland, its deputy president Ledum Mittee says from exile.
- Daughter of jailed activist Beko Ransome-Kuti plans fresh appeals to military ruler General Sani Abacha to free her father.
- Royal/Dutch Shell Group team from The Netherlands to begin from Sunday a five-day tour of Ogoniland as part of conciliatory moves.
- Military ruler Abacha intervenes over alleged 1.12 billion naira fraud at Federal Environmental Protection Agency (FEPA).
